package_info.why_malicious: The subdomain cdn2.cocoapods.org, previously used by CocoaPods for hosting package resources, was abandoned but its DNS records continued to point to GitHub Pages. Attackers hijacked the subdomain by creating a GitHub Pages site and associating it with the domain, allowing them to serve arbitrary content (initially a casino website) from a trusted CocoaPods subdomain. This creates a high risk for malware distribution, phishing, or supply chain attacks targeting developers and automated systems that trust the CocoaPods domain.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when users or automated tools access cdn2.cocoapods.org (e.g., via browser or package manager fetches)
execution_context.file_location: cdn2.cocoapods.org (content hosted via GitHub Pages repository controlled by attacker)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Full HTML, JavaScript, and CSS content of a casino website, hosted on the hijacked subdomain. The content is attacker-controlled and can be replaced at any time with malicious scripts, phishing forms, or malware payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the hijacked subdomain serves attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript content to any client accessing cdn2.cocoapods.org, allowing the attacker to deliver arbitrary web pages, execute malicious scripts in the user's browser, or prompt for sensitive information, resulting in potential malware infection, credential theft, or supply chain compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Serving unrelated or attacker-controlled content from a trusted open-source infrastructure subdomain is highly suspicious, as it enables attackers to exploit user trust and deliver malicious payloads or phishing attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would be to serve only legitimate CocoaPods package resources or documentation; instead, the subdomain serves arbitrary, unrelated, and potentially harmful content controlled by an attacker.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve serving static assets or documentation for CocoaPods, but only when managed by the official project maintainers. Any content not related to CocoaPods and not managed by the project is abnormal.
key_indicators: Abandoned subdomain (cdn2.cocoapods.org) still resolving to a third-party hosting provider (GitHub Pages)
Content served is unrelated to CocoaPods (e.g., casino website, not package resources)
Ability for attacker to rapidly change hosted content to malware, phishing, or other malicious payloads
No official project control over the subdomain's content

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies that the subdomain cdn2.cocoapods.org is abandoned but its DNS records still point to GitHub Pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker recognizes an opportunity to claim the subdomain via GitHub Pages.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a GitHub Pages repository and configures it to serve content at cdn2.cocoapods.org, effectively hijacking the subdomain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains full control over the content served at the trusted CocoaPods subdomain.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads and serves arbitrary web content (initially a casino website, but could be replaced with malware, phishing pages, or malicious scripts).
attack_chain.leads_to: Users and automated systems accessing cdn2.cocoapods.org receive attacker-controlled content.

attack_chain.action: Attacker can further exploit the hijacked subdomain to distribute malware, conduct phishing attacks, or compromise the software supply chain by targeting developers and automated tools that trust the CocoaPods domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential user compromise, data theft, or supply chain compromise via trusted infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Trusted infrastructure subdomains (e.g., cdn2.cocoapods.org) serving content unrelated to their original purpose
Sudden change in content type or hosting provider for a known subdomain (e.g., from package resources to unrelated web pages)
Access to developer infrastructure domains resulting in unexpected or suspicious web content (e.g., casino, gambling, or phishing pages)
file_indicators: Presence of DNS CNAME or A records for infrastructure subdomains (e.g., cdn2.cocoapods.org) pointing to third-party hosting (such as GitHub Pages) without active project ownership
Unexpected HTML/JavaScript content on subdomains previously used for package distribution or documentation
network_indicators: cdn2.cocoapods.org responding with non-CocoaPods content (e.g., casino website, phishing forms, or unrelated scripts)
HTTP(S) requests to cdn2.cocoapods.org resulting in responses containing gambling, casino, or other unrelated keywords or assets
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor DNS records for critical infrastructure subdomains to identify those still pointing to third-party hosting services without active project control. Regularly scan and verify the content served from all subdomains of key domains (e.g., cocopods.org) for unexpected changes in content type or hosting provider. Alert on any trusted subdomain serving unrelated or suspicious content, and implement two-way validation for custom domain linking on hosting platforms to prevent unauthorized associations.
